items.narrative: The session is adopting msgpack as the primary serialization format. msgpack is a lightweight binary serialization protocol that trades some human readability for significant improvements in both serialization speed and payload size, making it well-suited for high-throughput systems and storage-constrained environments. This decision complements the other infrastructure choices already made in this session around performance optimization and security hardening.
items.facts: ["msgpack chosen as the serialization format","Selected for performance and space efficiency","Follows infrastructure decisions on caching (LRU with 300s TTL), password hashing (argon2id), and TLS (OpenSSL)"]

items.title: Adopt OpenSSL for TLS Implementation
items.subtitle: Chose OpenSSL as TLS library for proven stability and maturity
items.narrative: The team decided to use OpenSSL for TLS implementation in the system. OpenSSL was chosen for its maturity, widespread adoption, and proven reliability in production environments. This follows the earlier decision to adopt argon2id for password hashing, continuing a pattern of selecting well-established, battle-tested cryptographic libraries over newer alternatives.
items.facts: ["OpenSSL selected as the TLS implementation library","Decision rationale: tried and tested library with established track record","Replaces or confirms against alternative TLS library options"]

items.title: Adopt argon2id for password hashing
items.subtitle: argon2id selected for superior GPU and side-channel attack resistance
items.narrative: Decision made to use argon2id for password hashing operations. argon2id is a memory-hard key derivation function that resists both GPU acceleration attacks (through high memory requirements) and side-channel attacks (through constant-time operations). This represents an upgrade from simpler hashing approaches in the authentication system.
items.facts: ["argon2id chosen as password hashing algorithm","Provides protection against GPU-based brute force attacks","Provides protection against side-channel timing attacks"]

items.title: LRU Cache with 300-Second TTL
items.subtitle: Selected LRU cache with 300-second TTL for improved reasoning and simplicity
items.narrative: The session decided to use an LRU cache with a 300-second TTL for an upcoming implementation. This approach was preferred because it provides a cleaner and more straightforward mental model compared to alternative caching strategies, making the system easier to reason about and maintain.
items.facts: ["Cache implementation uses Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy","Time-to-live (TTL) set to 300 seconds","Design chosen for simplicity and clarity of reasoning over alternatives"]
